name: Weighted Pull-Up
description: Loaded vertical pull — the strongest direct transfer to steep climbing.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a weight belt or dumbbell between feet. Start with arms fully extended and shoulders engaged (scapulae depressed and slightly retracted). Pull until chin clears the bar with chest lifting toward the bar. Lower with a 2-3s eccentric to full hang. Keep legs long and core braced; avoid kipping.
time_efficient_variation: Cluster sets: 3 sets of 2 doubles with 20s intra-set rest.
age_considerations: For 50+ athletes cap load at bodyweight +25%; prioritize controlled eccentrics.
desk_worker_notes: Not a desk-worker issue directly; helps posterior chain overall.
injury_prevention_notes: Protect finger flexors with full warm-up; avoid crimp grip on load.
contraindications: ["active finger pulley injury","acute rotator cuff irritation"]
pt_rehab_relevance: Late-stage rehab for shoulder post-op once ROM and pain-free pull is re-established.
common_compensations: ["kipping hip drive","shrugging into ears","elbows flaring wide"]
image_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, Public domain, author: Extremistpullup at English Wikipedia

name: Hangboard Max Hang (20mm Edge)
description: Near-max isometric dead hang on a 20mm edge — the benchmark for finger strength.
instructions: After a thorough warm-up including 3-4 sub-maximal hangs, hang from a 20mm edge with a half-crimp or open-hand grip (never full crimp). Target hangs of 7-10 seconds at an intensity where you could hold 2-3 more seconds at most. Add weight via harness if bodyweight is too easy. Rest 2-3 minutes between hangs. Stop the session at the first sign of sharp finger pain.
cues: shoulders engaged — active hang, not passive
stop the set if form degrades
time_efficient_variation: Repeaters protocol (7s on / 3s off) substitutes in time-crunched training days.
age_considerations: 40+ start with an 18-20mm edge; avoid small edges under 14mm unless conditioned. 50+ prioritize volume over intensity.
desk_worker_notes: Counteracts forward-head and kyphotic desk posture via scapular engagement.
injury_prevention_notes: Absolutely no full crimp under load. Warm up fingers thoroughly before a max hang.
contraindications: ["active finger pulley injury (A2/A3)","flexor tendinopathy flare","shoulder impingement without active engagement"]
pt_rehab_relevance: Contraindicated during acute pulley rehab; valuable in late-stage tendon rehab under supervision.
common_compensations: ["shoulders shrugged into ears","passive hang (dead weight on joints)","full crimp under load"]
regression: Bodyweight dead hang on jug or 25mm edge.
progression: Heavy max hangs on 18mm edge; one-arm hangs.

name: Hangboard Repeaters (7/3 Protocol)
description: Strength-endurance protocol on a 20mm edge — six-set hang block.
instructions: On a 20mm edge, hang for 7 seconds, rest 3 seconds, repeat for 6 hangs = one set. Rest 2-3 minutes between sets. Do 3-6 sets. Intensity: by hang 6 you should feel you have 1-2 more hangs in the tank. Use the same half-crimp or open-hand grip throughout; do not switch grips mid-set.
cues: stop the set at the first failed hang
time_efficient_variation: Short session: 3 sets only on 60s rest.
age_considerations: 50+ use a larger edge (22-25mm) or jug to protect pulleys.
desk_worker_notes: Good post-desk shoulder and finger extensor activation when paired with antagonist work.
injury_prevention_notes: Avoid if fingers have been warm-started from climbing earlier in the day; recovery compounds.
pt_rehab_relevance: Late-stage PT progression for climbers returning from pulley injury.
common_compensations: ["shoulders shrug up on final reps","form breaks on hang 6"]

name: Lock-Off Hold (90°)
description: Isometric elbow-flexed hold at 90° — direct transfer to static climbing moves.
instructions: From a pull-up bar, pull up to a position where your elbows are bent 90° and chin is at bar height. Hold for 5-10 seconds with shoulders engaged and core tight. Lower under control. Progress by adding weight or by holding one-armed on the off-hand.
time_efficient_variation: One all-out hold per side between other work.
home_variation: Pull-up bar with eccentric lowers from the 90° position.
age_considerations: 40+ cap hold time at 5s; prioritize full ROM.
desk_worker_notes: Counters forward shoulder and reinforces scapular control.
common_compensations: ["shoulders shrug","hips swing","elbows creep up out of 90°"]

name: One-Arm Hang (Assisted)
description: One-arm dead hang with pulley or band assist — builds asymmetric finger strength.
instructions: Use a pulley-and-counterweight system or a large resistance band looped over the bar for assist. Start with ~30-40% bodyweight of assistance and reduce over weeks. Hang on one arm from a 20mm edge or jug for 5-10 seconds, shoulder engaged. Alternate arms. Always use the assist until comfortable with bodyweight one-arm on a jug.
cues: stop the rep before form breaks
time_efficient_variation: Drop to 3 sets per arm on rest days.
age_considerations: Not recommended under 40 unless experienced; 50+ skip unless competitive.
injury_prevention_notes: Progress gradually; one-arm loading magnifies pulley and shoulder risk.
contraindications: ["any active finger pulley injury","shoulder instability","rotator cuff strain"]
source_video_attribution: How To Do Assisted One Arm Hang (YouTube)
image_attribution: How To Do Assisted One Arm Hang (YouTube)

name: Front Lever Progression (Tuck / Advanced Tuck)
description: Straight-body hold parallel to the ground — core + pulling integration.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar or rings. Pull your knees to chest into a tuck, then lift hips and tilt back until torso and bent legs are horizontal. Hold the tuck for 5-15 seconds with lats engaged pulling the bar toward hips. Progress by extending legs (advanced tuck → one-leg → straddle → full).
cues: pull the bar toward your hips, not yourself toward the bar
time_efficient_variation: Three quality holds, one on each progression level.
home_variation: Rings or bar at home works.
age_considerations: Skip the full lever; tuck is plenty of stimulus.
progression: Advanced tuck → one-leg → full front lever.
source_video_attribution: How To Tuck Front Lever Tutorial (YouTube)
image_attribution: How To Tuck Front Lever Tutorial (YouTube)

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: Anti-extension core work — bridges strength and stability for climbing.
instructions: Start on knees with hands on the ab wheel, hips over knees. Roll the wheel forward keeping spine long and pelvis posteriorly tilted. Stop before your lower back extends. Pull back by driving hips forward and engaging lats.
home_variation: Any ab wheel or loaded barbell on plates.
age_considerations: 50+ start with half-rollouts to wall.
desk_worker_notes: Directly counters anterior pelvic tilt common in desk workers.
injury_prevention_notes: Stop the rep before the low back extends.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
description: Heavy horizontal pull — antagonist to vertical pulling patterns common in climbing.
instructions: Hinge at the hips to ~45° with a neutral spine and a barbell in a double overhand grip, hands just outside shoulders. Pull the bar to the lower sternum driving elbows back and squeezing shoulder blades. Lower with control to full arm extension.
time_efficient_variation: Pause-at-top rows: 3 sets of 6 with 2s pause at contraction.
home_variation: Dumbbell row or inverted row under a sturdy table.
age_considerations: 50+ prefer chest-supported rows to remove lumbar load.
desk_worker_notes: Excellent for counteracting desk-worker thoracic kyphosis and rounded shoulders.
injury_prevention_notes: Maintain hip hinge; do not round the lumbar spine.
contraindications: ["acute lumbar disc herniation","acute low back pain"]
pt_rehab_relevance: Strengthens mid-back for postural rehab.

name: Seated Cable Row
description: Horizontal pull with constant tension — climber-friendly daily-driver.
instructions: Sit with feet braced, knees slightly bent, and grip a close-grip or neutral handle on a cable machine. Start with arms extended, lats engaged. Pull the handle to the lower sternum, driving elbows back; squeeze the shoulder blades. Return under control.
cues: long arms at start, full stretch
time_efficient_variation: 2 sets at the top of the range with 3s pause.
home_variation: Banded row anchored to a low post.
age_considerations: Great for 50+ since there's no spinal loading.
desk_worker_notes: Directly addresses rounded shoulders.
pt_rehab_relevance: Foundational for mid-back / scap rehab.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Row
description: Unilateral row — corrects side-to-side imbalance common in one-sided climbers.
instructions: Place one knee and hand on a bench, torso parallel to the floor. Hold a dumbbell in the opposite hand with arm hanging. Row the dumbbell to the hip, driving the elbow up and back, without rotating the torso. Lower with control.
home_variation: Dumbbell at home or filled backpack.
age_considerations: Any age; excellent longevity lift.
desk_worker_notes: Counteracts dominant-side asymmetry and posture issues.
pt_rehab_relevance: Routine for shoulder and mid-back rehab.
regression: Bent-over row with light dumbbells, both arms.

name: Typewriter Pull-Up
description: Advanced pulling drill — pull to one side, shift across, lower.
instructions: From a pull-up bar, perform a pull-up and hold at the top with chin over bar. Shift your body laterally to bring your chin over one hand; pause. Shift across to the other hand; pause. Lower under control. This is one rep.
cues: elbow stays bent as you shift
age_considerations: 40+ may skip; this is joint-demanding.
injury_prevention_notes: Demands shoulder health; skip if shoulder is flagging.

name: Archer Pull-Up
description: Asymmetric pull-up — one arm does most of the work while the other extends to the side.
instructions: Grip the bar wide. Pull up toward one hand while the other arm stays extended and braces against the bar. Chin clears the bar near the working hand. Lower under control. Alternate sides.
home_variation: Home pull-up bar with wider grip.
age_considerations: 50+ stick with weighted pull-ups.

name: Push-Up
description: Primary antagonist pattern for climbers — pushing strength with scapular control.
instructions: Start in a plank with hands shoulder-width, shoulders over wrists, body in a straight line from head to heels. Lower chest to an inch off the floor with elbows tracking ~45° from the torso. Press back to plank, finishing with scapular protraction (push the floor away).
time_efficient_variation: 3 sets to 2 reps shy of failure.
age_considerations: Any age; incline for older athletes.
desk_worker_notes: Counters kyphotic posture via scap protraction at top.
pt_rehab_relevance: Early-stage push rehab.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
description: Loaded horizontal push — antagonist to pulling for climbers.
instructions: Lie on a bench holding dumbbells at chest height, elbows at ~45° from torso. Press the dumbbells up and slightly together until arms are fully extended (without locking or letting shoulders roll forward). Lower under control to chest level with dumbbells just wider than the rib cage.
home_variation: Floor press with dumbbells at home.
age_considerations: 50+ use a slight incline to offload the AC joint.
desk_worker_notes: Crucial for addressing climber push-pull imbalance.
common_compensations: ["elbows flare to 90","shoulders roll forward","back arches off bench"]

name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
description: Vertical push — the most neglected pattern for climbers.
instructions: Stand or sit tall with dumbbells at shoulder height, elbows slightly in front of the torso. Press overhead until arms are straight with biceps near ears. Maintain a braced core; ribs tucked (no excessive arching). Lower with control.
home_variation: Dumbbells or a kettlebell at home.
age_considerations: 50+ use neutral-grip dumbbells to reduce shoulder stress.
desk_worker_notes: Directly combats forward-head and kyphotic desk posture.
injury_prevention_notes: Stop if shoulder impinges; address mobility before loading.
pt_rehab_relevance: Late-stage rehab for pressing movements post-shoulder surgery.

name: Dips (Parallel Bar)
description: Bodyweight push-pattern — shoulder-intensive, use with care.
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars with arms straight, shoulders depressed. Lower with control by bending elbows and leaning slightly forward until upper arms are parallel to the floor. Press back up. Avoid going below parallel unless mobility allows.
time_efficient_variation: 2 sets to 2 reps shy of failure.
age_considerations: 40+ skip unless shoulders are healthy; 50+ prefer push-ups.
injury_prevention_notes: Do not go past parallel; this is the shoulder-unfriendly zone.

name: Reverse Wrist Curl
description: Forearm extensor strengthening — counters chronic climbing grip load.
instructions: Sit with forearm on a bench or thigh, palm down, hand hanging off the edge. Hold a light dumbbell with a relaxed grip. Curl the wrist upward extending the hand toward the ceiling. Lower slowly. Keep the forearm planted.
time_efficient_variation: Two supersetted sets with wrist flexor curls.
home_variation: Any light dumbbell or can of soup.
age_considerations: Excellent for all ages.
desk_worker_notes: Helps counter carpal tunnel / desk-related wrist flexor dominance.
injury_prevention_notes: Critical prehab for tennis elbow and forearm imbalance in climbers.
pt_rehab_relevance: First-line exercise for lateral epicondylitis rehab.
regression: Bodyweight finger extension on table edge.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up
description: Triceps-dominant push — targets locked-elbow positions common in climbing.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with hands directly under shoulders, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond-ish shape (or simply narrow). Lower keeping elbows tracking close to the torso until chest is an inch above hands. Press back up.
time_efficient_variation: 2 sets to 1 rep shy of failure.
age_considerations: Any age.

name: Landmine Press
description: Joint-friendly overhead push variation — excellent for older lifters.
instructions: Stand in a half-kneeling or standing stance holding the end of a barbell in a landmine attachment at shoulder height. Press the bar up and slightly forward until the arm is extended. Lower under control. Alternate arms.
age_considerations: Great for 40+/50+; offloads shoulder vs strict overhead press.
desk_worker_notes: Shoulder-friendly vertical pressing pattern.
injury_prevention_notes: Shoulder-friendly press that works around impingement.
pt_rehab_relevance: Common rehab progression for shoulder post-op or impingement.

name: Pike Push-Up
description: Bodyweight vertical push approximation — accessible overhead stimulus.
instructions: From a downward-dog pike position with hips high, lower the top of your head toward a point between your hands. Press back up until arms are straight. Keep hips high throughout. Progress by elevating feet.
time_efficient_variation: 2 sets to 2 reps shy of failure.
age_considerations: 50+ keep hips lower (less vertical); protects AC joint.
desk_worker_notes: Excellent mobility + antagonist combo.

name: Band Pull-Apart
description: High-frequency scap/posterior-delt work — daily antagonist mini-dose.
instructions: Stand with a light band held in both hands at shoulder height with arms extended. Pull the band apart by driving hands wide and squeezing shoulder blades together. Return under control.
time_efficient_variation: Two supersetted sets between other work.
age_considerations: All ages.
desk_worker_notes: Daily-driver fix for rounded shoulders.
pt_rehab_relevance: First-line exercise for shoulder posture rehab.

name: Triceps Extension (Dumbbell, Overhead)
description: Long-head triceps work — supports lock-offs and pushing.
instructions: Stand or sit tall holding a single dumbbell overhead with both hands cupping the top end. Lower the dumbbell behind the head by bending only at the elbows (upper arms stay vertical). Extend back overhead.
time_efficient_variation: 2 sets to 2 reps shy of failure.
age_considerations: Any age.
desk_worker_notes: Balances heavy pulling volume.

name: Face Pull (Cable or Band)
description: External rotation + scap retraction — both antagonist and prehab.
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a cable at face height (or loop a band). Grip the rope with thumbs pointing back. Pull toward the face with elbows high and wide, ending with hands near ears and shoulder blades squeezed. Pause. Return under control.
time_efficient_variation: 2 sets with 2s hold at end range.
home_variation: Banded version anchored to a door.
age_considerations: Any age — gold-standard posture lift.
desk_worker_notes: Top exercise for reversing forward-shoulder desk posture.
injury_prevention_notes: Highest-yield shoulder prehab movement; program daily-ish.
pt_rehab_relevance: First-line rehab for shoulder impingement and posterior cuff weakness.
common_compensations: ["shrug into ears","elbows drop","using lats instead of rear delts"]

name: Scapular Push-Up
description: Scap-only push-up — serratus activation in the plank.
instructions: Start in a plank with straight arms. Without bending elbows, drop the chest by pinching shoulder blades together; then push the upper back toward the ceiling by protracting the scapulae. Keep the body straight throughout.
age_considerations: All ages.
desk_worker_notes: Great serratus activation for desk-bound shoulders.
pt_rehab_relevance: Rehab for winging scapula and serratus weakness.

name: Prone Snow Angel (Y-T-W-L)
description: Scapular control flow — complete posterior shoulder activation.
instructions: Lie face-down on the floor with arms overhead. Move through 4 positions: arms overhead (Y), arms out to sides (T), elbows bent 90° (W), arms by hips with palms up (L). Raise each position an inch or two off the floor, hold 2s, lower. 5 reps per position = one round.
age_considerations: All ages; excellent for older athletes.
desk_worker_notes: Reverses the rounded shoulder desk pattern.
injury_prevention_notes: Daily-driver shoulder prehab.
pt_rehab_relevance: Rehab for posture, mid-back weakness, and early rotator cuff issues.
common_compensations: ["lifting with lumbar extension","using traps instead of mid-back"]

name: Scapular Retraction (Prone W)
description: End-range scapular retraction with externally rotated arms.
instructions: Lie face-down with arms bent 90° forming a "W", palms facing forward, thumbs up. Lift the arms off the floor by squeezing the shoulder blades down and back. Hold 2 seconds. Lower.
age_considerations: All ages.
desk_worker_notes: Direct antidote to rounded-shoulder desk posture.
pt_rehab_relevance: Common for scap dyskinesis and rounded-shoulder rehab.
source_video_attribution: YouTube (Prone W T Y Scapular Retraction)
image_attribution: YouTube (Prone W T Y Scapular Retraction)

name: Campus Board Ladder (1-3-5)
description: Max-effort contact strength on a campus board — reserved for advanced climbers.
instructions: Fully warm up: dynamic shoulder mobility + easy climbing + sub-max hangs. On a campus board with evenly-spaced rungs, start matched on rung 1. Move the leading hand up to rung 3, then the trailing hand to rung 5. Reverse down. Rest 3 minutes between reps. 3-5 reps is a full session.
age_considerations: 40+ approach cautiously; 50+ avoid unless lifelong climber.
injury_prevention_notes: Highly joint-demanding; never campus fatigued or with any finger flag.

name: Explosive Pull-Up
description: Concentric-focused pull-up aiming for max bar speed.
instructions: Set up like a strict pull-up. Pull as fast as possible so that the chest comes to the bar or higher. Lower under control for 1-2 seconds. Rest fully between reps.
cues: hands leave bar only if doing bar clapping
age_considerations: 40+ use controlled speed vs max velocity.
injury_prevention_notes: Shoulders must be healthy; avoid if impinging.
regression: Fast concentric pull-up without bar clearance.

name: Box Jump
description: Lower-body power expression — useful for dynamic climbing foundations.
instructions: Stand in front of a plyo box 1-2 feet away. Load the hips by dropping into a quarter squat, then explode upward, swinging the arms, and land softly on top of the box with feet flat and knees slightly bent. Stand tall. Step down (do not jump down).
age_considerations: 40+ reduce box height; 50+ swap to step-ups.
injury_prevention_notes: Always step down to protect the Achilles.
contraindications: ["achilles tendinopathy","acute knee pain","active lumbar disc issue"]
common_compensations: ["jumping down (Achilles risk)","hips collapse on landing","box too tall (causes hip flexion compensation)"]

name: Medicine Ball Slam
description: Full-body rotational-free power output.
instructions: Stand holding a slam ball or soft med ball overhead. Extend up tall, then rapidly contract the core and drive the ball into the floor in front of you. Pick it up and repeat.
age_considerations: Any age with a durable ball.
common_compensations: ["pulling the ball with arms only","lumbar flexion under load"]

name: Dynamic Lock-Off (Campus-Lite)
description: Pull-up + lock-off + controlled release — builds contact strength.
instructions: From a pull-up bar, pull into a chest-to-bar position, hold 2s, release one hand to a briefly lower position before re-catching. Alternate sides. Build to deeper releases over weeks.
age_considerations: 40+ use light releases; 50+ stick with lock-offs.
injury_prevention_notes: Prerequisite: clean one-rep-max weighted pull-ups.

name: Broad Jump
description: Horizontal power output — ground-reaction training.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width. Load the hips into a quarter squat with arms back; explosively extend hips and swing arms forward to launch as far as possible. Land softly with bent knees.
age_considerations: 40+ shorter jump distance; 50+ skip unless athletic history.

name: Rowing Erg Intervals
description: Full-body cardio without joint impact — good option on climbing rest days.
instructions: Warm up for 3 minutes easy. Perform 4-6 rounds of 500m hard (RPE 7-8) with 90-120s easy rowing between. Cool down 3 minutes.
age_considerations: All ages.
desk_worker_notes: Improves aerobic base that supports long climbing sessions.

name: Hangboard Repeaters (Endurance Variant)
description: Sub-maximal long repeater protocol — finger endurance for sport/trad.
instructions: On a 20mm edge or larger, hang for 10 seconds / rest 5 seconds, repeat for 6 hangs = one set. Rest 1 minute between sets. Do 4-6 sets. Intensity should stay sub-maximal — you could do 2 more hangs at the end of each set.
age_considerations: 50+ use jug or larger edge.
pt_rehab_relevance: Endurance-phase finger rehab progression.

name: Barbell Back Squat
description: Primary bilateral lower-body compound — general athletic foundation.
instructions: Unrack a loaded barbell onto the upper traps. Set feet ~shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Brace the core and descend by breaking at the hips and knees together, pushing the knees out over the toes. Descend to at least parallel. Drive through the feet to stand up.
time_efficient_variation: Two hard sets with 3 reps in reserve.
age_considerations: 50+ use box squat to control depth and reduce load.
desk_worker_notes: Reinforces hip and thoracic mobility lost to sitting.
injury_prevention_notes: Off-season priority; in-season reduce volume 40%.
pt_rehab_relevance: Late-stage rehab after most lower-body injuries.

name: Romanian Deadlift (Barbell)
description: Hip-hinge with minimal knee bend — hamstring and posterior chain foundation.
instructions: Hold a barbell at the hips, feet hip-width. Soften knees slightly (10-15° bend). Hinge at the hips by pushing the hips back, keeping the bar close to the legs and the spine neutral. Lower until you feel a hamstring stretch (usually mid-shin). Drive hips forward to stand.
home_variation: Dumbbells or kettlebell hinge at home.
age_considerations: 50+ use dumbbells to reduce lumbar load.
desk_worker_notes: Counters seated hip flexor dominance.
injury_prevention_notes: Neutral spine at all times; do not round.
contraindications: ["acute lumbar disc herniation","acute low back pain"]
pt_rehab_relevance: Rehab for hamstring injuries in late stage.
common_compensations: ["lumbar flexion","knees bend too much","shoulders shrug forward"]

name: Conventional Deadlift
description: Hip-hinge pull from the floor — ultimate full-body strength lift.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width, mid-foot under the bar. Hinge down and grip the bar just outside the shins. Flatten the back, brace hard, pull the slack out of the bar. Drive through the feet and stand up with the bar close to the body. Reverse by hinging at the hips first.
age_considerations: 50+ use trap-bar or sumo for reduced lumbar shear.
injury_prevention_notes: Off-season priority; avoid within 72h of heavy climbing.
contraindications: ["acute lumbar disc herniation","acute low back pain","hernia"]
common_compensations: ["rounding lumbar","bar drifts from body","jerking the bar"]

name: Goblet Squat
description: Front-loaded squat with a dumbbell or kettlebell — the best squat regression.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height with both hands cupping the top. Feet shoulder-width. Descend by breaking at hips and knees to at least parallel. Keep chest up and elbows down. Drive back up.
age_considerations: Any age — one of the best longevity lifts.
desk_worker_notes: Opens hips and thoracic spine.
pt_rehab_relevance: Rehab progression after lower body injury.

name: Kettlebell Swing
description: Posterior-chain-dominant ballistic hip hinge — power-endurance foundation.
instructions: Stand with a kettlebell an arm's length in front. Hinge to grip it with both hands. Hike it back between the legs, then snap the hips forward to launch the bell to chest height. Let it fall by hinging, redirect with a hike pass, repeat.
cues: snap the hips at the top
age_considerations: 50+ start with lighter bells and focus on hinge mechanics.
common_compensations: ["squatting the swing","using arms to lift","lumbar flexion"]

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: Unilateral knee-dominant — fixes side-to-side leg imbalance.
instructions: Stand a stride's-length in front of a bench. Place the top of the back foot on the bench. With or without dumbbells, descend by bending the front knee until the front thigh is parallel to the floor. Drive through the front foot to stand.
age_considerations: 50+ reduce depth; use chair for balance.
pt_rehab_relevance: Late-stage knee rehab.

name: Pallof Press
description: Anti-rotation core — foundational for any rotational sport.
instructions: Set a cable or band at chest height, anchored to one side. Stand perpendicular to the anchor. Hold the handle at the sternum with both hands. Press straight out to arms extended; hold 2s; return. Resist the rotational pull throughout.
home_variation: Banded at any anchor at home.
age_considerations: All ages.
desk_worker_notes: Core stability for any desk-posture user.
injury_prevention_notes: Top anti-rotation exercise.
pt_rehab_relevance: Core rehab for lumbar spine.

name: Farmer's Carry
description: Loaded carry — total-body tension, grip, postural endurance.
instructions: Hold heavy dumbbells, kettlebells, or trap bar at sides with a strong grip. Stand tall, ribs down, shoulders packed. Walk 40-60 feet with strict posture. Rest. Repeat.
cues: stand tall — crown of head up
age_considerations: All ages.
desk_worker_notes: Great for sedentary workers — builds postural endurance.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
description: Glute-max dominant posterior chain lift — cornerstone for cyclists, runners, and change-of-direction athletes.
instructions: Sit with upper back against a bench, feet flat, barbell over hips. Drive hips up until shoulders, hips, and knees are in a straight line. Squeeze glutes hard at the top. Lower under control.
home_variation: Dumbbell hip thrust or single-leg hip thrust at home.
injury_prevention_notes: Knee and hip drivers for cyclists/runners; prehab for hamstring strains.
progression: Single-leg hip thrust or heavier loads.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
description: Eccentric hamstring exercise — single most protective intervention against hamstring strains in running/soccer.
instructions: Kneel on a pad with ankles anchored (partner or strap). Hinge at the knees, lowering torso toward the floor as slowly as possible. Catch with hands. Push back up with arms; repeat.
home_variation: Ankles under a couch with pad; partner hold.
injury_prevention_notes: Top-tier hamstring strain prevention.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
description: Unilateral glute activation — cornerstone for any runner with a knee or IT-band history.
instructions: Lie on back, one knee bent 90°, other leg extended. Drive through the planted heel to lift hips, keeping pelvis level. Lower under control. Complete reps; switch sides.
injury_prevention_notes: IT-band / PFPS prehab; unilateral glute control.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: Unilateral hinge — hamstring/glute strength plus balance.
instructions: Stand on one leg, slight knee bend. Hinge at the hips, extending the back leg behind like a counterweight. Lower until the torso is parallel-ish to the floor. Return by squeezing the planted glute.
cues: torso and back leg form a line
injury_prevention_notes: Excellent unilateral hamstring prehab.

name: Single-Leg Heel Drop (Eccentric)
description: Eccentric-focused calf work — the Alfredson protocol for Achilles health.
instructions: Stand on a step with the ball of one foot, heel off the edge. Rise to double-leg calf raise. Shift weight to one leg and slowly lower that heel below the step level over 3 seconds. Use the other leg to return to the top.
injury_prevention_notes: Gold-standard Achilles rehab protocol.
progression: Loaded single-leg heel drop with dumbbell.

name: Standing Calf Raise
description: Bilateral gastroc strength.
instructions: Stand on a step or flat floor. Rise onto the balls of the feet as high as possible. Pause. Lower slowly to full range.

name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
description: Rotational power output for golfers, tennis players, baseball — anywhere hips drive the swing.
instructions: Stand sideways to a wall, 3-5 feet away, holding a med ball at chest height. Rotate away then explosively rotate through the hips and throw the ball into the wall. Catch the rebound and repeat.

name: Cable Wood Chop (High-to-Low)
description: Diagonal anti-rotation and rotational-power pattern — functional carry-over to rotational sports.
instructions: Set a cable at high position. Standing perpendicular, grip the handle with both hands at the high side. Drive the handle across and down to the opposite hip by rotating the torso — hips follow, not the other way around. Return under control.
home_variation: Band anchored high to a door.

name: Shrimping / Hip Escape
description: BJJ fundamental movement — also a mobility staple for all grapplers.
instructions: Lie on back, feet flat. Elevate hips and shoot them back and to one side, shrimping the hip away from an imaginary opponent. Plant one foot, push with the shoulder/forearm, shift hips, and repeat down the mat.
injury_prevention_notes: Foundational grappling movement.

name: Turkish Get-Up
description: Full-body ground-to-standing loaded movement — THE kettlebell exercise for grapplers.
instructions: Lie on back holding a kettlebell vertically in one hand, arm locked out. Roll up to a seated position, then to a knee, then stand, keeping the weight overhead throughout. Reverse the sequence to return. Switch sides.
injury_prevention_notes: Full-body rehab and shoulder stability.

name: Bear Crawl
description: Quadrupedal locomotion — core, shoulder, and coordination for all grapplers.
instructions: Start in a crawl position: hands under shoulders, knees under hips, knees hovering an inch off the floor. Crawl forward moving contralateral arm and leg together.
progression: Bear crawl with drag or sled push.
image_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — Airman 1st Class Kayla Newman (Public domain)

name: Neck Bridge (Wrestler's Bridge)
description: Isometric neck strengthening — essential for wrestlers and BJJ athletes, controversial for novices.
instructions: Lie on back with feet flat, hands supporting near the head. Slowly raise hips and arch onto the top of the head, bearing some weight on the neck, some on hands. Start with hands carrying most load. Progress very gradually.
injury_prevention_notes: Neck strengthening for contact sports; progress gradually. Contraindicated with any cervical pathology.
regression: Neck isometrics with hands only (no bridge).

name: A-Skip Running Drill
description: Dynamic running mechanics drill — knee drive and foot strike.
instructions: From standing, skip forward driving one knee up to hip height with dorsiflexed foot. Opposite arm swings forward. Strike down-and-back with the ball of the foot. Alternate legs in a rhythm.

name: Wall Sit
description: Quad-endurance isometric — useful for cyclists, skiers, and hikers.
instructions: Lean against a wall with feet out far enough that when you slide down, thighs are parallel to the floor and knees at 90°. Hold position. Breathe.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Rotation
description: Rotational strength in a narrow base — translates directly to rotational sports.
instructions: Half-kneel perpendicular to a cable column, cable at chest height. Grip the handle with both hands at the near shoulder. Rotate the torso away from the cable, pressing out. Return under control.

name: Single-Leg Squat to Box
description: Unilateral knee-dominant strength — ski/snowboard cornerstone.
instructions: Stand on one leg in front of a box, bench, or sturdy chair. Sit back to tap the box with the hip, extending the opposite leg forward for balance. Return to standing by driving through the planted foot.
injury_prevention_notes: Knee stability for skiing, snowboarding, trail running.

name: Eccentric-Focused Back Squat (Skier Prep)
description: Back squat with a 4-5s eccentric — ski-specific quad eccentric load.
instructions: Standard back squat, but descend over 4-5 seconds under full control. Stand back up at normal tempo.
cues: brace hard on the way down
injury_prevention_notes: Ski-specific quad eccentric prep.

name: Split Squat Jump
description: Single-leg explosive power — advanced plyo for ski, skating, running.
instructions: Drop into a lunge position. Explosively jump, switching legs mid-air, landing in the opposite lunge. Absorb the landing, then repeat.
injury_prevention_notes: Ski/running explosive power. Avoid with acute knee or ankle pain.
image_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0, author: RickyBennison

name: Hollow Hold
description: Gymnastic anti-extension hold — total trunk tension.
instructions: Lie on back. Press low back flat. Lift arms and legs a few inches off the floor, keeping the low back pressed. Hold.

name: Side Plank
description: Anti-lateral-flexion core — critical for runners and rotational athletes.
instructions: Lie on side with elbow under shoulder, legs stacked. Lift hips so body forms a straight line from feet to head. Hold. Breathe.
injury_prevention_notes: Lumbar spine support.

name: Inverted Row
description: Horizontal bodyweight pull — home-friendly row alternative.
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at hip height (or use a sturdy table). Lie underneath, grip the bar shoulder-width, body straight. Pull the chest to the bar by driving elbows down and back. Lower under control.
home_variation: Barbell in rack or sturdy table edge.

name: Lat Pulldown (Straight-Arm)
description: Straight-arm pulldown on cable — isolates the lat for the pulling phase of the freestyle stroke.
instructions: Face a cable machine with handle set high. Grip a straight bar or rope with straight arms. Keep arms straight and pull the bar down to the hips by driving the lats. Return under control.

name: Dolphin Kick (Poolside / Dryland)
description: Dryland mimicry of the dolphin-kick pattern — hip mobility + core coordination.
instructions: Lie face-down on a bench with legs extended off the end. Perform a controlled dolphin kick pattern from the hips. 30 seconds per set.
cues: kick from the hips, not knees

name: Wall Ball Shot
description: Full-body conditioning movement — squat + press combo with a med ball.
instructions: Hold a med ball at chest height. Squat to parallel, then explosively stand and throw the ball to a target ~9-10 feet up on the wall. Catch the rebound at chest height and flow into the next squat.

name: Box Jump Over
description: Plyo box jump with additional lateral traversal — CrossFit-style conditioning.
instructions: Jump onto the box, then step or jump down on the opposite side. Turn around and repeat. Maintain quiet landings.

name: Double-Under (Jump Rope)
description: Jump rope with two rope passes per jump — CrossFit conditioning staple.
instructions: Jump with a jump rope, rotating the wrists fast enough that the rope passes under the feet twice per jump.

name: Burpee
description: Full-body conditioning move combining squat, plank, push-up, jump.
instructions: From standing, drop to a plank via squat. Perform a push-up. Jump feet forward, then explode up into a small jump. Repeat.
image_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, Public domain, author: Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Ryan Young

name: Power Clean
description: Olympic lifting derivative — pulls a barbell from the floor to the shoulders in a quarter squat.
instructions: Set up with a barbell over mid-foot, hip hinge to grip. Explosively extend hips, knees, and ankles while shrugging the shoulders. Drop into a quarter squat and catch the bar on the front deltoids.

name: Superman Hold
description: Prone hold with arms/legs lifted — builds the posterior-chain extension essential for freestyle body position.
instructions: Lie face-down, arms extended overhead. Lift the chest, arms, and legs off the floor simultaneously. Hold for 15-45 seconds. Breathe throughout.
progression: Add light dumbbells or longer hold.

name: Flutter Kick (Hollow)
description: Hollow-body flutter kicks — swim-specific core + hip flexor endurance.
instructions: Lie supine, low back pressed into the floor. Legs straight, raised a few inches. Alternate small fast up-down kicks from the hips. 30-60 seconds per set.
cues: kick from the hips not the knees

name: Med Ball Shot Put
description: Rotational power throw mimicking the serve motion.
instructions: Stand sideways to a wall. Hold a med ball at the shoulder (as if about to shot-put). Rotate hips and push the ball into the wall with an explosive press. Catch rebound and repeat.

name: Cossack Squat
description: Deep lateral squat — hip mobility + unilateral strength for lateral court movement.
instructions: Stand with wide stance. Shift weight over one leg, lowering into a deep side squat with the other leg straight. Stand up and shift to the opposite side in a flowing movement.
cues: knee tracks over toes on the bent side

name: Lateral Lunge
description: Side lunge — adductor strength and lateral court movement prep.
instructions: Stand tall. Step out to one side into a wide lunge, bending the stepping-side knee while the other leg stays straight. Push back to center. Alternate sides.

name: Lateral Shuffle / Agility Line
description: Side-to-side footwork drill — essential for reactive court/field movement.
instructions: Stand in an athletic stance between two lines ~4-6 feet apart. Shuffle rapidly side-to-side, touching each line. 20-30 seconds per bout.

name: Cross-Over Step
description: Court-movement drill — crossover step for rapid direction change.
instructions: Stand sideways to your target. Push off the outside foot and drive the inside leg across the body, rotating hips and running 3-5 steps. Reset. Alternate directions.

name: Squat Jump (Counter-Movement)
description: Vertical counter-movement jump — athletic power baseline.
instructions: Stand tall. Quickly drop into a quarter squat, then explode straight up as high as possible. Land soft with bent knees.

name: Depth Jump
description: Reactive plyo — drop from height, absorb, immediately jump vertically for explosive reactive strength.
instructions: Stand on a 12-18" box. Step off (do not jump off). On landing, spend as little ground-contact time as possible and explode vertically into a max jump.

name: Tuck Jump
description: Vertical jump with tucked knees to chest — explosive leg power + core.
instructions: Stand tall. Quickly drop and explode upward, tucking the knees to the chest at apex. Land soft and repeat.

name: A-Skip to Sprint
description: Acceleration drill — starts with A-skip rhythm, then transitions to full sprint.
instructions: Start with 5-10m of A-skips (high knee drive, dorsiflexed foot). On the coach's call — or after a set number of skips — transition to a 10-20m max-effort sprint.

name: Copenhagen Adductor Lift (Dynamic)
description: Dynamic version of Copenhagen plank — adductor strength under movement, key for soccer/hockey.
instructions: Set up as for Copenhagen plank. From lifted position, lower the bottom hip toward the floor and re-lift with control. 5-8 reps per side.

name: Loaded Step-Up
description: Weighted step-up — hiking/mountaineering's signature prep exercise.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at sides or a barbell on the back. Step up onto a 12-18" box with one foot. Stand tall on top. Lower with control. Complete all reps on one leg before switching.

name: Downhill Step-Down (Eccentric)
description: Slow eccentric step-down — targets the quad eccentric demand of long descents.
instructions: Stand on a 6-12" step with one leg. Slowly lower (3-5s) the other leg to tap the floor, controlling the descent entirely with the standing leg. Return to standing. Complete reps; switch sides.

name: Rucking (Zone-2 Walking with Pack)
description: Walking under a loaded pack — specific to mountaineering and multi-day backpacking.
instructions: Wear a weighted pack (20-30% bodyweight). Walk at Zone-2 pace for 30-90 minutes on varied terrain. Keep posture tall; adjust pack if it swings.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise (Eccentric, Loaded)
description: Loaded eccentric calf raise — builds tendon resilience for long descents and rough terrain.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in one hand, stand on the ball of the same-side foot on a step. Rise to full calf raise with both feet, then shift weight and slowly (3-5s) lower the loaded-side heel below the step.
cues: use off-side leg to return to top
image_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — No machine-readable author provided. GeorgeStepanek assumed (based on copyright claims). (CC BY-SA 3.0)

name: Neck Harness Extension (Four-Way)
description: Plate-loaded or harness-resisted neck strengthening in all four directions — essential for grapplers and strikers who absorb head contact.
instructions: Using a neck harness or hand resistance, work flexion, extension, and both lateral flexions in turn. 8-12 slow reps each direction. Load is light — this is tendon and slow-twitch work, not a max lift.
home_variation: Towel + partner or bodyweight manual resistance.

name: Plate Pinch Hold
description: Two-plate pinch grip hold — builds the pinch-grip endurance needed for gi lapels, wrist control, and clinch.
instructions: Stack two smooth-sided plates (10-25 lb each). Pinch them together at the top with one hand, thumb on one side, fingers on the other. Stand tall and hold as long as possible up to 45 seconds. Alternate hands.
cues: squeeze hard, don't let the plates slip
home_variation: Stack of books or heavy hardcovers pinched.

name: Fat-Grip Dead Hang
description: Thick-bar dead hang — forearm and grip endurance closer to the grip demands of a gi sleeve or wrist.
instructions: Wrap a thick-grip attachment around a pull-up bar (or hang on a 2.5"+ bar). Hang with shoulders engaged. Target 20-45 seconds. Rest fully between sets.
home_variation: Towel draped over a bar for the same effect.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
description: Unilateral hip thrust — the lift that mirrors bridging, scrambling out of bottom, and sprawling to one side.
instructions: Upper back on a bench, one foot planted, other leg lifted. Drive the grounded heel into the floor and lift hips until hip, knee, and shoulder form a straight line. Squeeze glute hard at top. Pause 1s. Lower with control.
home_variation: Bodyweight on floor with foot on low box.
progression: Loaded single-leg hip thrust with DB on hip.

name: Kettlebell Clean (Single-Arm)
description: Kettlebell clean — explosive hip hinge that teaches the sprawl-to-stand and takedown-reversal timing.
instructions: Start with KB between feet. Hike pass into a single-arm clean, catching the bell in the rack position. Lower under control to a relaxed swing between the legs. Repeat. 5-8 reps per side.
cues: catch soft — no banging the wrist
progression: Double KB clean or clean + jerk.

name: Banded Hip Thrust (Home)
description: Band-resisted hip thrust for the home gym — same pattern as barbell hip thrust, portable setup.
instructions: Sit with upper back against a couch or bench. Loop a heavy band over hips, anchored under both feet (or a heavy object). Drive hips up, squeezing glutes at top. Lower under control.

name: Landmine Rotation
description: Landmine rotational anti-extension with ballistic finish — core rotation under load, specific to punching and clinch work.
instructions: Stand holding the end of a landmine barbell at chest height with both hands. Keep elbows slightly bent and feet wide. Rotate the bar from one hip to the other by pivoting the back foot and driving from the hips. Pause each side. 6-10 reps per direction.
cues: arms are long levers, not pumps
home_variation: Barbell in a corner + weight on end.

name: Cable Punch / Chest Press Rotation
description: Single-arm cable press with rotation — mimics the mechanics of a straight punch with resistance through the full extension.
instructions: Stand in a staggered stance facing away from a cable stack at chest height. Hold the handle in the back-side hand at the shoulder. Punch forward and across the body, rotating the torso and back hip as you extend. Return under control. 8-10 per side.
cues: fast on the punch, controlled return
home_variation: Resistance band anchored behind for home.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
description: Supine pullover — opens the lats and chest while strengthening the serratus/lat connection that strikers and grapplers both underuse.
instructions: Lie supine on a bench, feet flat. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, arms extended over the chest. Keep a slight bend in the elbows and lower the weight back over the head until you feel a strong stretch in the lats/chest. Return to start.
cues: feel the stretch, don't force it

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
description: Floor press — a strength press that protects the shoulder and removes the bottom-range vulnerability (boxing, MMA shoulder health).
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent. Press dumbbells from the chest to full extension. Triceps touch the floor on the eccentric — this halves the shoulder stretch range compared to a bench.
progression: Heavier DBs or single-arm floor press.

name: Heavy Bag 3-Minute Round
description: Three-minute heavy bag round — sport-specific striking conditioning that blends technique, power, and cardio.
instructions: Work the bag for 3 minutes at a sustainable striking pace (not max power — glycolytic threshold). Mix jabs, crosses, hooks, teeps, and combinations. 1 minute rest. 3-6 rounds total.
cues: hands back to guard every strike
home_variation: Heavy bag or shadowboxing if no bag.

name: Sled Push 3-Min Round
description: Loaded sled push for a 3-minute round — alactic/lactic conditioning that matches a round structure and builds drive-phase leg power.
instructions: Push a moderately loaded sled for short (10-20 yd) bursts. Walk back. Continue for 3 minutes. 1 minute rest. 3-4 rounds. Load should allow steady effort, not failure.

name: Zercher Good Morning
description: Front-loaded good morning — posterior chain strength in a grappler-specific trunk position (loaded chest, hip hinge).
instructions: Hold a barbell in the crook of the elbows (Zercher). Feet shoulder-width. Hinge at the hips with a slight knee bend, keeping the chest up and spine neutral. Return by driving through the hips.

name: Sandbag Bear Hug Carry
description: Loaded bear hug carry — awkward-object conditioning that mirrors controlling a grip in clinch, bear hug, or top position.
instructions: Pick up a sandbag in a bear hug at chest height. Walk 30-50 feet maintaining posture. Reset and repeat for time or distance.

name: Lateral Bound to Stick
description: Lateral plyo — pushes off one leg, lands on the other, sticks — trains the side-to-side push-off of stance changes and slips.
instructions: Stand on one leg. Explosively push off laterally, landing on the opposite leg in athletic stance. Stick the landing for 2s before rebounding. 5-6 per direction.
cues: knee tracks over toes on landing

name: Prone T Raise
description: Prone horizontal abduction — isolated mid-trap and posterior-delt work to counter racquet-swing internal-rotation bias.
instructions: Lie face-down on a bench or floor, arms out to the sides in a T position with thumbs up. Squeeze the shoulder blades and lift arms off the floor to shoulder height. Pause. Lower slowly. 10-12 reps.

name: Bent-Over Reverse Fly
description: Bent-over dumbbell reverse fly — direct posterior-delt and rhomboid load.
instructions: Hinge forward from the hips with a flat back, dumbbells hanging below shoulders. Lift both arms out to the sides to shoulder height while squeezing the shoulder blades. Pause, then lower. 10-15 reps.
progression: Heavier DBs or pause at top.

name: Landmine Rotational Press
description: Rotational landmine press — full kinetic chain, racquet-swing-specific loaded rotation.
instructions: Hold the end of a landmine bar at shoulder height with both hands, weight to one side. Rotate the hips and press the bar up and across the body to the opposite side. Return under control. 6-8 per side.
home_variation: Landmine or barbell in a corner.

name: Cable High-to-Low Chop
description: Cable chop from high to low across the body — mimics the downward-strike phase of the forehand and smash.
instructions: Set a cable pulley high. Stand sideways, grip the handle with both hands. Chop down and across the body to the opposite hip, rotating through the torso. Return with control. 10-12 per side.

name: Cable Low-to-High Lift
description: Cable lift from low to high across the body — mirrors the topspin forehand drive and open-stance strokes.
instructions: Set a cable pulley low. Stand sideways, grip the handle with both hands. Lift up and across the body to the opposite shoulder, rotating through the torso. Return with control. 10-12 per side.

name: Depth Drop to Stick
description: Step off a box and absorb the landing — dedicated deceleration training without the reactive jump-up of a depth jump.
instructions: Stand on a 12-18" box. Step off (don't jump). Land with both feet, immediately stick the landing: knees bent, hips back, chest up, quiet feet. Hold the landing 2-3 seconds. Step off and reset. 4-6 reps.

name: Agility Ladder Icky Shuffle
description: Fast in-in-out ladder drill — footwork quickness and coordination for racquet court movement.
instructions: Set up an agility ladder. Step in-in-out pattern: left foot in, right foot in, left foot out to the side. Next square: right-left-right out. Move through the length of the ladder quickly. 3-4 passes.
cues: light on the balls of your feet

name: 5-10-5 Pro Agility Shuttle
description: Change-of-direction shuttle — gold standard test of COD for court sports.
instructions: Set three cones 5 yards apart in a line. Start at the middle cone. Sprint 5 yards to one side, touch the line, sprint 10 yards to the far cone, touch, sprint 5 yards back through the middle. 3-4 runs per direction.

name: Lateral Step-Down (Eccentric)
description: Slow eccentric lateral step-down — quad and glute-med control for sharp lateral court braking.
instructions: Stand on a 6-10" step on one foot, other leg hanging off the side. Slowly (3-4s) lower the hanging foot to the floor by flexing the standing hip and knee. Return to start. 8-10 per side.

name: Split-Stance Iso Hold
description: Wall-supported split-squat isometric hold — pre-event-safe knee and quad loading.
instructions: Set up in a split stance with the back foot elevated on a bench (or on the floor), torso upright, hands against a wall for support if desired. Lower to ~90° front knee. Hold 20-30 seconds. 3-4 holds per side.
image_attribution: Wikimedia Commons — U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Myles Stepp (Public domain)

name: Single-Arm Cable Paddle Pull
description: Standing single-arm cable row that mimics the catch-and-pull of a paddle stroke — primary dryland strength builder for paddlers.
instructions: Stand square to a mid-height cable with a single handle. From a staggered stance, reach the handle forward (catch), then pull past the hip with a rotating torso, driving the elbow back. Control the return. 8-12 reps per side.
cues: rotate the torso, don't just arm-pull
home_variation: Swim cords or resistance band anchored low.

name: Landmine Rotational Row
description: Bent-over row into the landmine with a rotational finish — trains the pull+rotate pattern under load.
instructions: Straddle a landmine barbell. Hinge at the hips, grab the bar sleeve with one hand. Row the bar toward the ribs while rotating the torso slightly open. Lower under control. Alternate sides or complete all reps one side first.
home_variation: DB single-arm row with slight rotation.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
description: Row performed prone on an incline bench — removes low-back involvement and isolates upper-back for pulling volume.
instructions: Lie chest-down on a 30-45° incline bench. Let dumbbells hang at arm's length. Row both dumbbells to the ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Lower under control.
home_variation: Single-arm DB row with bench support.

name: Renegade Row
description: Plank + alternating dumbbell row — anti-rotation core plus pulling strength, the exact demand of paddleboarding.
instructions: Start in a plank with hands on dumbbells, feet wide. Row one DB to the ribs while keeping hips square to the floor. Lower, switch sides. Avoid twisting the hips.
home_variation: Bodyweight plank rows on household objects.
progression: Heavier DBs or add push-up between rows.

name: Cable Low-to-High Chop
description: Diagonal rotational pull from low anchor to overhead — mimics the paddle catch lifting out of the water.
instructions: Anchor a cable low. Stand sideways to the stack, grip with both hands at hip. Pivot the back foot and drive the handle diagonally up and across to the opposite shoulder. Return slow and controlled.
home_variation: Band anchored to a low post.

name: Kneeling Pallof Press with Rotation
description: Tall-kneeling Pallof press that adds a small trunk rotation — bridge between anti-rotation and rotation for paddlers.
instructions: Tall-kneel perpendicular to a cable at chest height. Press the handle away from the chest; then slowly rotate the torso 20-30° toward the stack and back. Return the handle to the chest.
cues: rotate through the spine, not the hips
home_variation: Banded Pallof press with small rotation.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: Hanging knee/leg raise — strong core and grip endurance, directly transferable to paddling posture control.
instructions: Hang from a bar with a full grip. Without swinging, raise the legs (bent or straight depending on ability) to at least hip height. Lower slow.

name: Dragon Flag (Tuck)
description: Tucked dragon flag on a bench — advanced anti-extension core for surfers and SUP racers.
instructions: Lie on a bench, grip behind the head. Brace the core, lift the body off the bench in a tuck position (shoulders remain planted), then lower slowly controlling the hips.
regression: Hanging leg raise as progression lead-in.

name: Bent-Arm Bar Hang
description: Isometric pull-up hold — pulling endurance for long paddling sessions.
instructions: Pull up until the chin is over the bar and hold. Keep breathing. Drop when form breaks. 15-30 seconds.

name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Rotation
description: Half-kneeling rotational drive through the landmine — hip-driven rotation is the paddle stroke's engine.
instructions: Half-kneel perpendicular to the landmine. Hold the bar sleeve with both hands at one shoulder. Drive the bar across the body to the opposite shoulder by rotating through the torso. Return slow.
cues: rotate the torso, not the knees
home_variation: Cable rotational chop as equipment swap.
source_video_attribution: Advanced Therapy Performance / Dr. Josh Heenan (YouTube)
image_attribution: Advanced Therapy Performance / Dr. Josh Heenan (YouTube)

name: Single-Leg RDL with Rotation
description: Single-leg RDL with a torso rotation at the bottom — hip-hinge balance and rotational stability for surfers/SUP.
instructions: Stand on one leg with a DB in the opposite hand. Hinge forward on the standing leg until the torso is parallel. At the bottom, rotate the torso slightly open. Return to standing.
progression: Heavier load or add pause at bottom.

name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat (Surf Stance)
description: Bulgarian split squat held in the surf stance — heavy quad/glute prep for the pop-up landing.
instructions: Place rear foot on a bench, front foot 2-3 feet ahead. Lower into a deep split squat, then drive up. Hold DBs for load.
progression: Heavier DBs or add a pause.

name: Scapular Wall Slide
description: Wall slide — scap upward-rotation drill and shoulder flexion mobility for paddlers.
instructions: Stand with back against a wall, arms in goalpost position. Slowly slide the arms overhead, keeping the forearms and low back in contact with the wall. Return.
progression: Add a band between the wrists.

name: Ski-Erg Intervals
description: Ski-erg intervals — upper-body pulling conditioning that crosses over strongly to paddling.
instructions: Warm up 5 minutes. Perform 5-8 intervals of 60 seconds at 85% effort, 60 seconds rest. Cool down 5 minutes.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Chop (High-to-Low)
description: Diagonal chop from high to low in a half-kneeling stance — core + hip stability for paddlers and surfers.
instructions: Half-kneel perpendicular to a cable anchored high. Grip the handle with both hands at the high-side shoulder. Chop diagonally down and across toward the opposite hip. Control the return.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust on Bench
description: Single-leg hip thrust — glute strength critical for pop-up drive and stance stability.
instructions: Upper back on a bench, feet on floor. Extend one leg straight. Drive through the planted heel to lift the hips to full extension. Lower slow.
cues: squeeze the glute at the top

name: Reverse Nordic Curl
description: Kneeling quad-eccentric — builds the rectus femoris length-under-load that sprinters and soccer players need to avoid hip-flexor and quad strains.
instructions: Kneel with knees hip-width apart, feet pointed. Keep the body rigid from knees to head. Slowly lean backward by extending the hips, reaching as far back as quads allow. Return to upright with control.
progression: Add a load (plate at chest) or deeper lean.
source_video_attribution: Eccentric Quad Exercise / Reverse Nordic Curl (YouTube)
image_attribution: Eccentric Quad Exercise / Reverse Nordic Curl (YouTube)

name: Lateral Deceleration Drill
description: Sprint-and-stop footwork drill — teaches safe lateral deceleration, the most common ACL-injury mechanism in soccer and basketball.
instructions: Set two cones 8-10 yards apart. Accelerate laterally toward one cone, then decelerate into a wide athletic stance (hips back, knees bent, chest up). Hold for a 1-count. Reset and repeat.
home_variation: Two cones or markers on any field.
regression: Slower walkthrough of the stop position.
progression: Add a partner cue or reactive direction change.

name: Prone Y-T-W-L Complex
description: Lower-trap + rotator-cuff complex — four-position posterior-shoulder builder, the workhorse for overhead sports.
instructions: Lie face-down on a bench or floor. In sequence: arms overhead Y, out to sides T, elbows bent W, then L (90°elbow, rotate up). 8-10 of each, moving continuously.
progression: Light DBs (1-3 lb) or slower tempo.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Lift
description: Anti-rotation lift in half-kneeling — builds the diagonal chain (hip to opposite shoulder) used in throwing and batting.
instructions: Half-kneel with the outside knee down, cable anchored low to that side. Grip the handle with both hands. Lift the handle diagonally across the body up to overhead on the opposite side. Control the return.
cues: initiate from the core, not arms
progression: Heavier load or standing cable chop variant.

name: Med Ball Chest Pass (Explosive)
description: Horizontal chest pass for explosive upper-body push — basketball outlet pass and football pushing power.
instructions: Stand 6-10 feet from a wall. Hold a med ball at the chest. Explosively push the ball into the wall with both hands, extending fully. Catch the rebound and repeat without pause.
progression: Heavier ball or single-arm shot-put variant.

name: Front Squat (Barbell)
description: Upright-torso barbell squat with front-rack load — quad-dominant strength that preserves a tall posture valuable for athletes.
instructions: Set the bar in a front rack (elbows high). Step back from the rack. Descend to at least parallel with knees tracking over toes. Stand tall. Reset.
cues: chest tall all the way down
progression: Heavier front squat or tempo pause.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
description: Hex-bar deadlift — athlete-friendly deadlift variation that hits quads and posterior chain without the spinal demand of a barbell pull.
instructions: Stand inside a hex bar. Hinge and grip handles. Set a neutral spine, drive through floor to stand tall. Lower under control.
progression: Heavier trap bar or paused deadlift.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Fly
description: Horizontal shoulder abduction with dumbbells — posterior deltoid and mid-trap strength for posture and antagonist balance.
instructions: Hinge at hips with dumbbells hanging. Keeping slight elbow bend, raise DBs out to the sides until arms parallel to floor. Lower with control.

name: Single-Arm Landmine Row
description: Single-arm row with a landmine — anti-rotation loaded pull, the team-sport core-and-back combo.
instructions: Set a barbell in a landmine. Straddle the sleeve facing away. Hinge and grip the sleeve in one hand. Row the barbell up while resisting torso rotation. Lower under control.

name: Cone Cutting Drill (T-Drill)
description: Four-cone T-shape cutting drill — multi-planar agility combining forward sprint, lateral shuffle, and backpedal.
instructions: Set cones in a T (top bar 10 yards, stem 10 yards). Sprint stem to middle cone, shuffle right to end cone, shuffle across to opposite cone, shuffle back to middle, backpedal to start.
cues: don't cross feet on the shuffle

name: Agility Ladder In-Out
description: Agility-ladder footwork drill — fast-feet training for basketball, soccer, and hockey footwork.
instructions: With an agility ladder flat on ground, move through with the in-in-out-out pattern (both feet in each square, then both feet out straddling). Work length of ladder, reset.

name: Dot Drill (5-Dot)
description: Five-dot reactive footwork drill — foot-speed, quickness, and coordination for all team sports.
instructions: Tape 5 dots in an X pattern (four corners + center, ~18" apart). Hop through patterns (front-back, side-side, scissor) for 10-15 sec per round.

name: Rope Skip (Speed Rope)
description: Speed jump rope — calf and ankle reactive conditioning, cheap and travel-friendly for any team-sport athlete.
instructions: With a speed rope, skip for 30-60 sec rounds. Stay on the balls of the feet, small hops, fast rope tempo. 3-5 rounds.
regression: Shorter rounds or no rope (ghost rope).

name: Drop to Vertical Jump
description: Step-off from a box immediately into a max vertical jump — reactive-strength primer before full depth jumps.
instructions: Stand on a 6-12" box. Step off. On landing, immediately jump vertically for max height. Aim to minimize ground-contact time.

name: Skater's Step-Down (Eccentric)
description: Slow eccentric step-down emphasizing knee control during deceleration — protects skater knees.
instructions: Stand on one leg on a 6-12" box. Over 3-4 seconds, slowly lower the other leg to tap the floor, controlling with the standing leg. Return to standing.

name: Push-Up Plyo (Wrist Fall Prep)
description: Reactive push-up — builds upper-body shock tolerance for the inevitable skater fall.
instructions: From a push-up position, explosively push off the floor so hands leave briefly. Land softly with slightly bent elbows and repeat. Progress to clap push-ups.
progression: Clap push-up or deficit plyo push-up.

name: Weighted Carve Squat
description: Rotational squat with torso rotation — mimics pumping/carving on a skateboard/surfboard.
instructions: Hold a light DB or plate at chest. Squat to parallel while rotating the torso toward one knee. Stand and rotate to the other knee on the next rep.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: Gymnastics-standard core hold — full-body compression essential for handstands and levers.
instructions: Lie supine. Press low back into the floor. Lift shoulders and straight legs 4-6 inches off the floor. Arms overhead. Hold 20-45 seconds.
regression: Tuck hollow or hands at sides.

name: Arch Body Hold (Reverse Hollow)
description: Posterior-chain counterpart to the hollow — trains the front-lever and back-line extension gymnasts need.
instructions: Lie prone. Arms overhead. Lift arms, chest, and legs simultaneously into a reverse banana. Squeeze glutes. Hold 20-45 seconds.

name: Tuck L-Sit Progression
description: L-sit foundation — hip-flexor and core compression for calisthenics.
instructions: Sit on the floor or parallettes with hands planted. Depress shoulders and lift both knees tucked toward the chest, hips off the floor. Hold 10-20 seconds.
regression: Support on blocks; feet on the floor.

name: Handstand Wall Hold
description: Wall-supported handstand — foundational inversion for gymnasts, yogis, calisthenics athletes.
instructions: Kick up to a handstand with the belly facing a wall or back against a wall. Stack shoulders over wrists. Hold 20-45 seconds. Focus on active shoulders and stacked body.

name: Ring Dip (False Grip Optional)
description: Gymnastics-ring dip — essential pushing strength for muscle-up and ring work.
instructions: Hang at the top of rings with straight arms, rings turned out. Lower the body until shoulders are just below the rings. Press back up with control.

name: Muscle-Up Transition Drill
description: Chest-to-bar high pull + transition — specific drill for the calisthenics muscle-up.
instructions: From a dead hang, perform an explosive pull that brings the chest above the bar. At the peak, drive elbows back and transition over the bar into a dip support.
cues: turn the elbows at the top

name: Depth Landing (No Rebound)
description: Drop from height and absorb silently — landing mechanics for parkour and gymnastics.
instructions: Step off a 12-24 inch box (do not jump). Absorb the landing with quiet feet, knees tracking toes, and hips back. Stick the landing completely silently.

name: Body Row (Rings or Bar)
description: Inverted row on rings — horizontal pull strength that scales endlessly for pole and calisthenics.
instructions: Hang under a set of rings or a bar with straight body, heels on the floor. Pull chest to the rings, retracting scaps first. Lower with control.

name: Pike Compression Lift
description: Seated pike leg lift — compression strength for L-sits, V-sits, and pole inverts.
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs extended in a pike. Hands flat next to hips. Lift straight legs as high as possible while keeping a pike position. Hold 1-2 seconds, lower.

name: Yogi Push-Up (Chaturanga)
description: Yoga-specific tricep push-up with elbows tight — key repeated pattern in vinyasa practice.
instructions: From plank, shift slightly forward. Lower slowly keeping elbows tight to the body until upper arms are parallel to the floor. Pause, then flow to up-dog or push back up.

name: Wall Walk (Handstand Approach)
description: Walk the feet up a wall into handstand position — builds inversion confidence and shoulder endurance.
instructions: Start in push-up facing away from wall. Walk feet up the wall while hands walk toward the wall until reaching handstand. Reverse.

name: Relevé Calf Raise (Ballet)
description: Ballet-style relevé — full-range calf raise onto the balls of the feet, key for all dance forms.
instructions: Stand tall, heels together in first position (or parallel). Rise onto the balls of the feet as high as possible while staying tall. Lower with control.
cues: rise to the ball of the big toe

name: Single-Leg Relevé with Balance
description: Unilateral relevé held on one leg — balance + calf strength for pointe work and turns.
instructions: Stand on one leg. Rise onto the ball of the foot and hold 5-10 seconds. Lower with control. Switch sides.

name: Single-Leg Bridge (Dance)
description: Single-leg hip bridge — posterior-chain strength for jumps and takeoffs in dance.
instructions: Lie supine, one foot flat, other leg extended. Drive through the heel, lift hips while keeping pelvis square. Lower with control. 10-12 per side.

name: Grand Battement (Kick Prep)
description: Ballet-style high kick — hamstring and hip-flexor power for dance.
instructions: Stand with one hand on a wall/barre. Kick the free leg forward as high as possible with a straight knee and pointed foot. Lower with control. 8-10 per direction per side.
cues: kick from the hip, not the back

name: Single-Leg Hop (Dance Tempo)
description: Single-leg rhythmic hop — plyometric base for Irish, hip-hop, contemporary.
instructions: Hop on one leg for 10-20 reps in place, emphasizing quiet feet and tempo. Switch legs.

name: Yoke Walk
description: Loaded yoke carry — strongman signature for full-body stiffness under heavy axial load.
instructions: Step under a loaded yoke with the pad across the upper traps. Brace hard, stand up, walk 40-60 ft with short controlled steps. Set down with control.
home_variation: Barbell in high-bar rack position as substitute.
regression: Barbell back carry at half weight.

name: Tire Flip
description: Large-tire flip — hybrid deadlift-clean-push movement central to strongman and highland games event prep.
instructions: Squat low to the tire with chest against it, hands under the bottom edge. Drive through the legs to lift and rotate, then transition the hands and push the tire over. Walk around and repeat.

name: Sled Push (Heavy)
description: Heavy prowler / sled push — leg-drive strength with near-zero eccentric cost, ideal for strongman and football carryover.
instructions: Set the sled with heavy load. Grip the posts with arms long, body at a strong forward lean. Drive through big powerful steps, full leg extension each stride. Push 30-50 ft. Rest 2-3 min.
home_variation: Push a loaded car in a safe lot.

name: Overhead Plate Peasant Carry
description: Single-plate overhead carry — shoulder stability + core endurance under axial load.
instructions: Press a single weight plate overhead with straight arms. Lock out the elbows, ribs stacked over pelvis. Walk 30-50 ft maintaining lockout. Set down, rest, repeat.
regression: Lighter plate or double-DB front rack.

name: Kettlebell Clean-and-Jerk EMOM
description: High-volume kettlebell clean-and-jerk conditioning — kettlebell sport competition staple.
instructions: With a moderate kettlebell in each hand (or one arm at a time), perform clean-and-jerks on the minute, every minute for 5-10 minutes. Start with 4-6 reps per minute; target competition pace (6-10/min).
regression: Short EMOM (3 min) with lighter bell.

name: Belt Squat
description: Loaded squat with load hanging from hips — heavy lower-body work with zero spinal compression.
instructions: Step onto the platform with a loaded belt clipped to hips. Squat to full depth keeping torso upright. Drive through mid-foot to stand. The load hangs below, not on the shoulders.

name: Safety-Bar Squat
description: Back squat with SSB — reduces shoulder ROM demand while loading the posterior chain heavily. Standard powerlifting accessory.
instructions: Unrack the safety bar across the upper back with hands on the padded handles. Brace and squat to depth, driving elbows forward to prevent a chest dump. Stand tall.

name: Snatch Balance
description: Barbell drops into overhead squat from behind-the-neck position — Olympic weightlifting positional drill for receiving the snatch.
instructions: Bar on the back with a wide snatch grip. Dip the knees slightly, drive the bar up while dropping into an overhead squat, catching with locked-out arms in a full squat. Stand with the bar overhead.
home_variation: PVC pipe for technique work at home.
progression: Heavier load or from the drop.

name: Hang Power Clean
description: Clean from the hang position (mid-thigh) caught in a partial squat — builds triple extension without the pull from the floor.
instructions: Set up with feet hip-width, bar at mid-thigh, chest up, shoulders slightly in front of the bar. Drive the hips forward powerfully and shrug, pulling under the bar to catch it on the front rack in a quarter squat. Stand tall.
cues: catch high in the partial squat
progression: Full squat clean from the hang.

name: Preacher Curl
description: Biceps isolation with humerus fixed on preacher bench — removes body english and isolates the biceps stretch.
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench, arms draped over the pad, elbows pinned. Hold an EZ-bar or dumbbells with a supinated grip. Curl to full flexion, then lower slowly to near full extension.
cues: full range, don't bounce out of the bottom
home_variation: Standing DB curl against a wall (elbows pinned).

name: Skull Crusher (Lying Triceps Extension)
description: Lying triceps extension — direct triceps stretch and isolation, bodybuilding staple.
instructions: Lie supine on a bench holding an EZ-bar or dumbbells overhead with arms vertical. Keeping elbows fixed, lower the weight toward the forehead (or just past). Extend back to vertical.
cues: lower to forehead then past ears
progression: JM press or heavier skull crusher.

name: Cable Crossover
description: Standing cable chest fly — horizontal adduction with constant tension; bodybuilding chest isolation.
instructions: Stand centered between two high cable pulleys. Grab a handle in each hand with a slight forward lean. Pull hands together in front of the hips in a hugging arc. Squeeze at the bottom; return slowly.
home_variation: Band crossover from a door anchor.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: Side-raise for the lateral deltoid — the signature shoulder isolation lift in bodybuilding.
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides, slight forward tilt. Raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height, leading with the elbows. Pause, lower slowly. Stop before the top-out if the traps take over.
cues: ride the lateral delts — don't swing
image_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0, author: Everkinetic

name: Block Pull (Deadlift off Blocks)
description: Deadlift pulled from 2-4 inch blocks — reduces range of motion, allowing heavier supramaximal loading. Powerlifting staple.
instructions: Set the barbell on blocks 2-4 inches off the floor. Set up as for a conventional deadlift from the higher start. Pull with a powerful hip drive, lock out standing tall.
home_variation: Deadlift off plates stacked on the floor.
progression: Deficit deadlift or heavier block pull.

name: Stone-to-Shoulder
description: Atlas stone or heavy sandbag lifted from the ground to shoulder — strongman event-specific lift combining deadlift, clean, and shouldering.
instructions: Straddle the stone/sandbag. Squat and wrap arms around it. Pull it onto the lap, then stand and continue the pull, rolling it up the chest and flipping it onto the shoulder. Alternate shoulders across sets.

name: Adductor Ball Squeeze (Supine)
description: Isometric adductor squeeze — trains the inner-thigh grip used to stay on the horse.
instructions: Lie supine with knees bent, a medicine or pilates ball between the knees. Squeeze the ball hard for 5-10 seconds, breathing throughout. Release partially, repeat.

name: Rider Wall Sit with Ball Squeeze
description: Isometric wall sit with a ball between the knees — mimics the position and inner-thigh demand of the saddle.
instructions: Sit against a wall at 90° knees and 90° hips. Place a ball between the knees and squeeze throughout. Hold for 30-60 seconds. Breathe and maintain posture.
progression: Longer hold or add DB held in front.

name: Landing Squat Absorption Drill
description: Low-height drop + absorb to a squat — trains the eccentric landing mechanics needed for paragliding/hang-gliding touchdowns.
instructions: Stand on a 6-12" box. Step off (don't jump). Absorb the landing softly into a quarter-squat with bent knees, immediately re-stabilize. Hold the landing for 2 seconds before stepping back up.

name: Archer Draw Isometric Hold
description: Band-simulated full-draw isometric hold — builds the upper-back endurance specific to archery anchor position.
instructions: Stand tall with a resistance band in the draw hand and the other arm extended toward the imaginary target. Draw the band to the anchor position (side of face/under chin). Hold the full-draw position 15-30 seconds.

name: Scapular Retraction Hold
description: Isometric scapular retraction hold — trains the endurance of the archer's back posture.
instructions: Either prone on a bench or standing with a band pulled apart at chest height. Pull the shoulder blades down and together, hold for 10-15 seconds. Release partially, repeat.

name: Sandbag Shoulder Carry
description: Heavy sandbag loaded on one shoulder — asymmetric loaded carry mimicking packing out game.
instructions: Hoist a heavy sandbag onto one shoulder. Walk 40-60 ft maintaining tall posture. Switch shoulders at the halfway point or on the next carry.

name: Reactive Start Drill
description: Start-on-cue explosive drill — handler-side speed for dog-agility and bikejoring starts.
instructions: Stand in an athletic stance. On a partner's or timer's cue, explode into a 10-15 ft sprint or first stride. Reset and repeat. Short, quality reps only.

name: Deceleration Drop-Step
description: Drop-step deceleration to change direction — critical for dog handlers and any reactive-sport athlete.
instructions: Jog 10-15 ft to a cone. At the cone, drop the outside foot back, sink into the hips, and explode in the new direction. Focus on quiet, absorbed steps.
cues: sink the hips on the drop

name: Overhead Sandbag Lockout Carry
description: Heavy sandbag pressed overhead and carried — strongman-style overhead stability under odd-object load.
instructions: Press a sandbag overhead with both hands, arms locked. Walk 30-50 ft maintaining lockout. Drop, rest 2 min, repeat.
cues: arms locked, biceps by the ears
short steps as load fights back
home_variation: Loaded duffel bag or plate overhead.

name: Wall Sit (Ski Tuck)
